title: Assemble a dental X-ray sensor holder: seat the arm's prongs in the bite block, then slide the aiming ring down the arm
instruction: Finish assembling the X-ray sensor holder: the arm seated in the bite block and the aiming ring down on the grip.
context: Dental assistants (O*NET 31-9091.00, 381,900 US jobs in 2024) and dental hygienists (29-1292.00, over 200,000 in dentists' offices alone, BLS May 2024) assemble this sensor holder before intraoral X-rays many times a day. Half-seated prongs or a ring whose centre line misses the sensor cause cone-cut images and retakes.
setup: Metres; world x forward, y left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases; table top z = 0.7475. (1) Tray slot, fixed: grey plastic recess holding the bite block's paddle with 0.3 mm play, 7.5 mm high walls 6 mm thick, and a 3 mm retaining lip over the paddle's far edge. (2) Bite block, free, 12 g, blue plastic, paddle-down in the tray slot, paddle centre (0.280, 0.020): 35 x 45 x 4 mm paddle, a sensor pocket on top (two 9 mm side rails with 2 mm lips), a 4 x 20 x 45 mm bite plate standing up from the paddle edge on the robot's right (toward -y), topped by a 12 x 20 x 20 mm connector block with two 3.2 mm square holes 8 mm apart, opening into an 8 x 16 mm lead-in over their top 3 mm. (3) Digital X-ray sensor, free, 20 g, black, 30 x 40 x 6 mm, in the pocket against the bite plate. (4) Arm stand, fixed, grey plastic, 30 x 24 x 30 mm, centre (0.200, -0.160), two 3.2 mm holes 18 mm deep. (5) Indicator arm, free, 20 g, stainless flat bar 5 x 2.5 mm: two 3 mm round prongs 18 mm long and 8 mm apart standing in the stand's holes, a crossbar running 31 mm from the prongs to an 85 mm upright, and a grey plastic grip hub 10 x 14 x 20 mm whose centre is 50 mm up the upright. (6) Aiming ring, free, 8 g, yellow plastic, lying flat at (0.370, -0.100): an annulus 46 mm inside, 60 mm outside, 5 mm thick; a lug from its rim carries a sleeve 22 mm tall with a 3.5 x 6.0 mm slot whose centre is 48 mm from the ring centre, and beyond it a 6 mm-thick, 12 mm-tall finger tab to 90 mm from the ring centre; the lug points back toward the robot and to its right (yaw -145 degrees). Friction (static/dynamic): bite block 0.4/0.35, sensor 0.5/0.45, arm 0.3/0.25, ring 0.4/0.35. Real-world parts: an obtainable Dentsply Rinn XCP-DS FIT kit measured before use, or the printable equivalent with 2.95 mm press-fit prong holes (holder_build/BUILD.md, STL files, make_parts.py).
scoring: Read at the end of the trial, and only once both grippers are at least 3 cm from the arm and the ring and the arm and ring have stayed still (under 0.5 mm per 50 ms step) for 1 s; otherwise 0. 0 if the bite block has tipped more than 5 degrees or moved more than 2 cm, or the sensor is more than 2 mm or 5 degrees out of its pocket position. 0.5: the indicator arm is seated: its prong tips within 1.5 mm (sideways and in depth) of fully home in the connector's holes, the arm within 8 degrees of upright. 1.0: in addition, the aiming ring is fitted: the upright passes through its sleeve (slot centre within 3 mm of the upright's axis), the ring rests on the grip hub (sleeve no more than 4 mm above the hub's top), level within 8 degrees, and the line through the ring's centre along its axis meets the sensor's plane within 10 mm of the sensor's centre (a standard 7 cm round cone then still covers the whole 30 x 40 mm sensor). Otherwise 0.
run_limit: 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo takes 803 steps
reset_notes: Stand the arm back in its stand by its prongs, lay the ring flat at its mark with the lug pointing back and to the right, and seat the bite block (sensor in its pocket) in the tray slot. Before a session check the prong press-fit with a push scale (5 to 15 N to seat; see holder_build/BUILD.md).
fidelity: Rigid parts built from boxes and plates; the ring is a 24-sided polygon. The prongs enter 3.2 mm holes (0.1 mm a side) with a moulded lead-in: rigid bodies cannot press-fit, so the real connector's light press-fit force (about 5 to 15 N in the printed equivalent) is not modelled. The bite block sits in a tray slot so one hand is free. The arm is a flat bar with a grip hub standing in for the ring's rest point. The X-ray beam is not simulated: aiming is the line through the ring's centre.
